title: Shanidar Cave Neanderthal burials
summary: Shanidar Cave in the Zagros foothills of Iraqi Kurdistan yielded the remains of ten Neanderthals in Ralph Solecki's 1951–60 excavations and more in Cambridge-led work since 2015. Whether some were deliberately buried, including the so-called flower burial of Shanidar 4, is debated; the remains date to roughly 75,000–45,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: Shanidar 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 are put at roughly 75,000 years ago and Shanidar 1, 3 and 5 at roughly 45,000–50,000 years; Shanidar Z at 70,000–60,000 years (preliminary).

as_recorded.value: Shanidar 1, 3, and 5 date to roughly 45,000–50,000 years ago

where.modern_name: Shanidar Cave, Erbil Governorate, Iraqi Kurdistan, Iraq
where.historical_name: Cave in the Zagros Mountains; no polities at this date

importance.justification: The cave shaped debate on Neanderthal care for the injured and mortuary behaviour.
